## Scope

This document specifies how www.ukeskywalker.com moves from Google Sites to a
Quarto site built from this repository and served by GitHub Pages. It covers
the song file format, the melody notation, the import from Google, the page
layout, the two tools, and the domain cutover.

Out of scope: audio playback, sheet-music rendering, user accounts, and any
editing in the browser. Songs are edited as text files in the repository.

## Current state

The sources, measured on 2026-10-19:

| Source | What it holds | Size |
|---|---|---|
| [Song sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1J4-ljjHTRQOX2olV-pJLCB6aqwrzKT2Yxj2s_01-tLM/edit) | One tab, `Songs`. One row per song with ratings; the title cell links to the song's Google Doc. | 254 rows, 229 distinct Google Doc links |
| Song Google Docs | Title line, often a key line and a YouTube link, then lyrics with inline chords such as `[G]`, and on many songs a melody after a tab. | 229 from the sheet, plus about 10 linked only from the site |
| [Google Site](https://sites.google.com/d/16YGbSXwlg8tCWyJs305TM0rLBXxvfWcW/p/1NsRxPE8a-rKKeuuVeW-j_OPPOHjXKz_E/edit) | Pages `/home`, `/compressor`, `/transposer`. The home page lists "Kids Songs with Dance Moves or Motions", "All Kid-Friendly Songs" and a "Songs to add" list. | 105 Doc links on the home page |
| This repository (before the move) | `index.html` and `compressTab.js`, an older copy of the chord compressor. | 2 files |

The sheet and both Google Docs sampled are readable without signing in, so the
import can run from a script with no Google credentials.

DNS today: `www.ukeskywalker.com` is a CNAME to `ghs.google.com` (Google
Sites); the bare domain points at GoDaddy forwarding addresses. The registrar is
GoDaddy.

## Site layout

The navbar, left to right:

| Tab | Page | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Songs | `index.qmd` | Every song, A–Z, in a searchable, sortable table |
| Libraries | menu | All Songs, Spiritual Songs, Andy Originals, Trendy Wendy and the Yeastbombs, Kid Songs, Sanctuary Boston Oct 2026 Retreat (a printable song sheet) |
| Compressor | `tools/compressor.qmd` | Chords-over-lyrics in, inline `[C]` chords out |
| Transposer | `tools/transposer.qmd` | Paste a song, pick a new key |
| About | page | `about.qmd`: what the site is, how to read a song page and the melody numbers. This specification is not in the navbar; it is at `specification.html` and in the repo. |

**Landing page: the full A–Z table.** Most visits are to find one song, and a
table with a search box finds it in one step. The library pages are the same
table filtered to one library. The table shows Song (linked to the song page),
Artist, Key, Difficulty and Added (the home page leaves out Difficulty), and each can be sorted. The rating columns
stay in the song files but are not shown; Quarto's table listing has no
show-or-hide toggle, so adding a column means adding it to the listing's
`fields:`.

**Search** comes in two forms, both built into Quarto:

- The box above each song table filters its rows by title, artist and key as
  you type.
- The magnifying glass in the navbar searches the full text of every page,
  lyrics included, so a half-remembered line finds its song. Quarto builds the
  index when the site renders; there is no server and nothing to maintain.

Directory layout:

```
_quarto.yml
index.qmd                 # A–Z table of all songs
specification.qmd         # this document
about.qmd
songs/<slug>.qmd          # one file per song
songs/files/<slug>.xlsx   # old spreadsheet arrangements, linked from the song page
_templates/song.qmd       # blank song with every field; copy to start a new song
_notes/                   # working notes kept in the repo, not on the site
libraries/<name>.qmd      # one listing page per library
libraries/sanctuary-boston-2026-10-retreat.qmd  # printable song sheet; its songbook: list names the songs
tools/compressor.qmd
tools/transposer.qmd
songs/_metadata.yml       # settings every song page shares: filter, CSS, scripts
_filters/song.lua         # turns the {.song} block and front matter into the page
_filters/song-render.lua  # {.song} block -> HTML, shared by song.lua and songbook.lua
_filters/songbook.lua     # builds a printable sheet from the songs it lists
assets/chords.js          # chord parsing and transposing, shared by tools and song pages
assets/song.js            # song toolbar: chords (inline/above/off), melody, key
assets/song.css           # screen and print layout for song pages
assets/songbook.css       # screen and print layout for printable sheets
assets/compressor.js
assets/transposer.js
styles.css                # site-wide styles
_scripts/import_sheet.py  # sheet -> data/songs.csv
_scripts/import_docs.py   # Google Docs -> songs/<slug>.qmd
_scripts/make_pdfs.sh     # prints each song sheet to PDF after rendering
data/songs.csv            # snapshot of the sheet, committed
data/raw/                 # raw Doc exports, not committed
data/import-report.md     # what the import could not read cleanly
data/import-hashes.csv    # what the import wrote, so it can tell hand edits apart
.github/workflows/publish.yml
```

## Song file format

Each song is one `.qmd` file in `songs/`, named by a slug of its title
(`banana-boat-song.qmd`). The metadata goes in the YAML front matter; the
lyrics, chords and melody go in one fenced block in the body.

A `.qmd` file is chosen over a bare `.yaml` file for two reasons. Quarto turns
each `.qmd` into a page with no extra code, and Quarto listings build the A–Z
table and the library pages straight from the front matter. A bare `.yaml`
file would need a generator script to make the pages, and the lyrics would sit
inside a YAML string, where indentation and colons cause errors.

### Front matter

```yaml
---
title: "Abigail, Belle of Kilronan"
sort_title: "Abigail, Belle of Kilronan"   # from the sheet, e.g. "Banana Boat Song, The"
artist: "Magnetic Fields"
key: G                  # key the song is written in below
alt_keys: [C]           # other keys offered as buttons, e.g. the one Andy sings in
youtube: ""             # full URL, or empty
libraries: [all]        # see "Libraries"
difficulty: 2           # sheet column Diffic.
practice: null          # 1–7: how much Andy wanted to practise it
fun: 3                  # 1–3: how fun it is to play
skill: 4                # how well Andy plays it
poppy: 3                # 1–3: how poppy
happy: 1                # 1–3: how happy
spiritual: null         # 1–3
protest: null           # 1–3
voice_low: E2           # Andy's voice: lowest note sung (sheet column Low)
voice_high: E3          # Andy's voice: highest note sung (sheet column High)
added: 2012-07          # sheet column Add_Date
pages: 2                # sheet column #pg
source_doc: "https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RWALFjB8i_oDnFNpQMQCjqDNSTxSTcnnQLAtvjtbRNI/edit"
other_links: []         # the sheet's Docs column: pdf links kept as links
files: []               # copies kept in the repo, e.g. [songs/files/apache.xlsx]
---
```

A blank sheet cell becomes `null`. Field names are lower case with
underscores so that Quarto listings can use them as column names. The sheet's
unnamed first column, an old page number for a PDF songbook, is not imported.

The rating fields (practice through protest) are imported and kept, but the
song tables do not show them by default. They cost nothing to keep, and a
sort by Fun or Happy can be added to the A–Z table later. Removing them all is
a one-line script if they turn out to be unused.

`voice_low` and `voice_high` are the lowest and highest notes Andy sings in
the song, in scientific pitch notation, where C4 is middle C and the number
goes up at each C. The song page shows them as "Andy's Voice: E2–E3". The
sheet writes them as `2 E`, `3A`, `4 C#`; the import turns `2 E` into `E2`.
Most rows fall between G2 and E4, a usual range for a lower male voice, which
suggests the sheet already used this numbering. The import lists every
converted value so a few can be checked against a piano or tuner app.

`source_doc` records where the song came from. After the move the Google Doc
is not read again; see "Import from Google".

### Template for a new song

`_templates/song.qmd` holds every field above with an empty value and a
comment saying what goes there, followed by an empty song block. To add a
song, copy it to `songs/<slug>.qmd` and fill in what you know.

Only `title` is required. Every other field may be left empty or deleted, and
the song page and tables skip a field with no value, so a song entered with a
title, artist and chords looks finished. The compressor's output (see "Tools")
is the same template with the song block filled in.

Files are excluded from rendering when their folder name starts with `_`, so
the template never appears on the site.

### Song body

The body holds one fenced block with the class `song`. Each line is lyrics
with inline chords, then optionally ` | ` and the melody for that line.

````
```{.song}
Verse 1:
[G] Abigail, can you feel my [C] heart in the [G] palm of your [D] hand | 3 2 1  1 1 1-2 3 4 6 6 5 4 3 2
and do you [Em] understand [C] why I can't sta-[G]-aa-[D]-aay        | 3 2 1 1 6. 6.-1  6. 1 2 3-2

Chorus:
When I come [C] home if I come [Em] home | 1 2 3 4  4 3 2 3
```
````

Rules:

- A chord is anything in square brackets: `[G]`, `[F#m]`, `[D/E]`. A run of
  chords with no lyric, such as `[G,F,C]`, is allowed.
- A line that ends in `:` and has no chords is a section label (`Verse 1:`,
  `Chorus:`, `Intro:`).
- A blank line separates stanzas.
- ` | ` (space, bar, space) separates lyrics from melody. The Google Docs use a
  tab for this, which the plain-text export turns into a run of spaces; the
  import splits at the first gap of three or more spaces that is followed by
  something melody-like (a digit, `(`, `+`), and writes ` | ` instead.
- Text after `#` at the start of a line is a note to the reader, shown in
  italics (`# Strum: D DU UDU`).

The lyrics-and-chords part of each line is already
[ChordPro](https://www.chordpro.org/) syntax, which many ukulele apps read, so
an export to `.cho` files later only has to drop the melody.

### Rendering

`_filters/song.lua`, a Pandoc filter that runs when Quarto renders, turns the
block into HTML: one row per line, each chord in its own element with the
original chord name kept in a `data-chord` attribute. The filter also puts the
artist under the title and a line of details above the song: key, Andy's
Voice, difficulty, YouTube, files, other links, and the song's libraries.
Rendering at build time means the site search indexes the lyrics as plain
text and the page reads correctly before any script runs.

`assets/song.js` then builds a toolbar at the top of every song page.

Built in phase 2:

- Lyrics on the left, melody in a narrower column on the right, one row per
  line, as in the Google Docs.
- **Melody switch** in the toolbar: on shows the melody column, off hides it.
  The choice is remembered in the browser, so it stays the same from song to
  song. Songs with no melody have no switch.
- A YouTube link under the title when `youtube` is set.
- A print stylesheet that drops the navbar and toolbar and fits most songs on
  one page. Printing follows the melody switch.

Built in phase 5, with the transposer, since both use `chords.js`:

- **Key menu** in the toolbar, showing the current key. It lists every key,
  with `key` and `alt_keys` at the top, plus − and + to step a semitone.
  Changing key rewrites the chords only; the melody is written in scale
  degrees, so it is the same in every key. Chords are spelled for the new key:
  flats in F, B♭, E♭ and the like, sharps in E, B and F♯, and in C, G, D and A
  sharps except B♭ and E♭.
- A chord is a root note and any suffix, so Andy's own marks (`C'`, `Fh`,
  `Bb*`, `Emx`) transpose by their root and keep the suffix. A bracket that
  does not start with a root (`[x]`, `[riff]`, `[Chorus]`) is shown as a
  note and not transposed.
- **Chords** buttons, first in the toolbar: Inline (`[G] Abigail`, the
  default), Above (chords over the lyrics) and Off (lyrics only). Off also
  hides lines that hold only chords and no melody. The choice is remembered
  in the browser, like the melody switch, and printing follows it.

With JavaScript off, the song shows with inline chords in its written key and
the melody column on.

## Melody notation

The melody uses numbered notation (in Chinese music, *jianpu*): each note is
a scale degree of the song's key.

| Written | Meaning | In the key of G |
|---|---|---|
| `1` … `7` | Scale degree in the middle octave | `1` = G, `3` = B, `5` = D |
| `6.` | One octave lower (a dot per octave) | `6.` = the E below the G |
| `1'` | One octave higher (an apostrophe per octave) | `1'` = the G above |
| `7m`, `3m` | Lowered degree; used in the Docs, read as a flat (to confirm) | `7m` = F, `3m` = B♭ |
| `#4`, `b7` | Raised or lowered degree (new; not yet in the Docs) | `#4` = C♯ |
| `1-2` | Notes sung on one syllable | |
| space | Next syllable | |
| two or more spaces | Phrase or word break, kept as written | |
| `0` | Rest (new) | |
| anything else | Kept as text, e.g. `(repeat)` | |

Rhythm is not encoded. The current Docs do not carry it, and adding it would
mean rewriting every melody by hand.

Because the melody is stored as text in a known notation, `song.js` can later show it as note
names in the current key (`1 2 3` in C reads `C D E`), with no change to the
file.

The import checks every melody token against this table and lists the ones
that do not fit: 38 lines across the songs on the first run. Most are
lower-case note names (`d e b g a c`) written in place of numbers, and a few
are chords or words that landed in the melody column. The Abigail Doc's second
copy, in C, has `6 e 5` where the first copy has `6 6 5`; that copy is dropped
by the import (the key menu replaces it), and the remaining lines are fixed by
hand.

## Libraries

A library is a value in the song's `libraries:` list. Each library page is a
Quarto listing of the songs that carry that value.

| Library | Value | First-pass rule from the sheet and site | Rows matched |
|---|---|---|---|
| All Songs | `all` | Every song | 260 |
| Spiritual Songs | `spiritual` | Spiritual column ≥ 1, plus songs Andy adds by hand | 60 |
| Andy Originals | `andy-original` | Artist is Andy Stein; three more added by hand | 10 |
| Trendy Wendy and the Yeastbombs | `yeastbombs` | Artist is Trendy Wendy and the Yeastbombs | 5 |
| Kid Songs | `kids` | Listed on the Google Site home page under "All Kid-Friendly Songs" or "Dance Moves or Motions" | 104 |
| (inside Kid Songs) | `kids-motions` | Listed under "Kids Songs with Dance Moves or Motions" | 18 |

The Kid Songs page shows two tables: songs with motions first, then every kid
song.

After the first pass, the `libraries:` list in each file is the record; the
rules above are not re-run. Adding a song to a library is a one-word edit.

A Quarto listing can filter on one value of a list field (tested: the
Spiritual Songs page lists exactly the 60 songs), so each library page is a
listing with `include: {libraries: <value>}`. "All Songs" in the menu is the
home page.

### Printable song sheet

The Sanctuary Boston Oct 2026 Retreat page,
`libraries/sanctuary-boston-2026-10-retreat.qmd`, prints four songs on one
sheet of paper, front and back: Love Will Hold Us Together on the front; The Rose, I've Got Peace Like a
River and This Little Light of Mine in two columns on the back. Its
`songbook:` front matter lists the printed pages and the song files on each,
so changing the songs is an edit to that list. `_filters/songbook.lua` reads
each song's file and prints it with chords and without the melody; a song
edit shows up on the sheet at the next render.

A Chords switch (on by default) hides the chords, the lines that hold only
chords, and the extra hyphen in words like `re-[Em]-member`. Print uses
whatever the switch shows. The publish workflow runs `_scripts/make_pdfs.sh`
after rendering, which prints the page with headless Chrome to
`sanctuary-boston-2026-10-retreat.pdf` and, with `?chords=off`, to
`sanctuary-boston-2026-10-retreat-lyrics.pdf`. The old address
`libraries/song-sheet.html` redirects to the page. The PDFs are not committed; locally, run the script after `quarto render` to make
them.

## Tools

**Compressor** (`tools/compressor.qmd`). Port of `compressTab.js`: paste chords
written above lyrics, get lyrics with inline `[C]` chords. Two changes from the
old code: the output also offers the full `{.song}` block with front matter,
so a new song from the web becomes a file in one paste; and the chord pattern
moves into `chords.js` so the compressor and transposer recognise the same
chords. The old loop also checked `i==s.length`, which is never true inside
the loop; the port fixes that end-of-text case. The old `/compressor` address
redirects here.

**Transposer** (`tools/transposer.qmd`). Paste a song in either format, choose
the from and to keys or a number of semitones, get the song back. It uses the
same functions as the key menu on song pages, so it spells chords the same
way. The Google Site's transposer code was not in this repository, so this is
a rewrite. Chord-only lines in chords-above-lyrics text are transposed in
place.

## Import from Google

Two scripts, run by hand, Python standard library only.

`_scripts/import_sheet.py` downloads the sheet as CSV (for the values) and as
`.xlsx` (for the `HYPERLINK` formulas behind each title), reads the Google
Site home page for its kid-song lists, and writes `data/songs.csv` with one
column per sheet column plus `doc_id`, `other_links`, `source` and
`libraries`. A song linked from the site whose title matches a sheet row with
no link gets that row's details; one with no match becomes a row of its own,
with `source` set to `site`. The CSV is committed.

`_scripts/import_docs.py` reads `data/songs.csv` and, for each row:

1. Downloads the Doc as plain text (`/export?format=txt`) into `data/raw/`.
2. Reads the title line (`Title - Artist`), a `Key of …` line, and any YouTube
   URL from the top of the Doc.
3. Converts the rest: the gap before the melody becomes ` | `, `’` in the
   melody becomes `'`, a line such as `Verse 1` becomes the label `Verse 1:`,
   and curly quotes become straight ones.
4. If the Doc has a second copy of the song below a `________________` line
   (as Abigail does, in C), keeps the first copy and adds the second copy's
   key to `alt_keys`.
5. Writes `songs/<slug>.qmd` with the front matter above.
6. Adds a line to `data/import-report.md` for anything it could not parse:
   melody tokens outside the notation, no key found, more than one copy, or a
   Doc that would not download.

Rows with no Google Doc still get a song page, with the details and links and
no song text: 28 songs on the first run.

The old spreadsheets are copied into the repository as Excel files, in
`songs/files/<slug>.xlsx`, and listed in the song's `files:` field. The song
page links to the file for download. These are grid layouts by time, with
instrument parts such as guitar, trumpet and melody in rows (Apache, Sweet
Dream), so they stay spreadsheets rather than becoming song blocks. Result on
2026-10-19, for the 15 songs with a spreadsheet link:

| Result | Count | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Downloads as `.xlsx` without signing in | 4 | The script saves them. |
| Refused (401): probably private to Andy's account | 10 | The script lists them in the import report; Andy downloads each with File → Download → Microsoft Excel while signed in, and saves it under the name the report gives. |
| Gone (410) | 1 | The link is kept with a note that the file no longer exists. |

The pdf links point at ukulelehunt.com, another person's site, so they stay as
links and are not copied.

Result of the first run on 2026-10-19: 260 songs (254 from the sheet, 6 only
on the Google Site), 233 Google Docs, of which 232 downloaded and 1 is
private. `data/import-report.md` lists 147 things to check, in 106 songs.

**After the import, the repository is the record and Google is retired.**
The song files are plain text that any editor can open and Quarto is open
source, so the site can move to any host if GitHub changes. New songs and
edits are made here, not in the Docs or the sheet. The import is a one-time
migration: once phase 3 is done, the script refuses to overwrite a song file
that has changed since it wrote it (it stores a hash of what it wrote in
`data/import-hashes.csv`), and `--force <slug>` re-imports one song if a
Google Doc turns out to have been read wrongly. After the cutover, the Google
Docs and the sheet get a line at the top pointing here.

## Hosting and the domain

GitHub Pages serves the site, built by a GitHub Actions workflow on every push
to `master`, the same pattern as the TrinityMetrics site: check out, set up
Quarto, render, upload `docs/` as the Pages artifact, deploy. The rendered
`docs/` folder is not committed.

The Google Site has three addresses people may have bookmarked. Quarto's
`aliases:` front-matter field writes a redirect page at each old address:

| Old address | New page |
|---|---|
| `/home` | `/` |
| `/compressor` | `/tools/compressor.html` |
| `/transposer` | `/tools/transposer.html` |

Cutover, in order:

1. Build and check the site at `https://iamstein.github.io/ukeskywalker/`.
2. In the repository's Pages settings, set the custom domain to
   `www.ukeskywalker.com`. With a GitHub Actions deploy, the setting is kept
   there and no `CNAME` file is needed.
3. In GoDaddy DNS: change `www` from `ghs.google.com` to `iamstein.github.io`;
   replace the bare domain's A records with GitHub's four
   (`185.199.108.153`, `185.199.109.153`, `185.199.110.153`, `185.199.111.153`).
   Remove any GoDaddy forwarding on the bare domain.
4. Wait for GitHub to issue the certificate, then tick "Enforce HTTPS".
5. In Google Sites, remove the custom URL from the old site. Leave the old
   site published for a month with a banner linking to the new one, then
   unpublish it.

## Phases

Status as of 2026-10-19. "Built" means it renders and was checked locally;
nothing is published yet.

| Phase | Work | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Skeleton | `_quarto.yml`, landing page, this spec, publish workflow; test listing filters on list fields | Site renders at the github.io address | Built. Needs a push and GitHub Pages set to "GitHub Actions". |
| 2. Format | Lua filter, `song.js`, `song.css`, template | Melody switch, YouTube link and print work | Built. Checked on Abigail and Annie Waits. |
| 3. Import | Both scripts; run on all rows; fix what the report lists | Every sheet row and site-only song has a page; report is empty or each line has a reason | Scripts run; 260 pages written. Report has 147 lines to work through, and 10 private spreadsheets to download. |
| 4. Lists | A–Z table with search box, five library pages, About | Each library's count matches the table in "Libraries"; navbar search finds a song from one lyric line | Built. Counts match; "palm of your" finds Abigail. |
| 5. Tools | `chords.js`; compressor and transposer pages; key menu and chord-layout switch on song pages | The old example compresses as before; Abigail moved to C matches the C copy in its Google Doc | Built and checked. |
| 6. Cutover | Domain steps above; delete `compressTab.js` | www.ukeskywalker.com serves this site over HTTPS; `/home` and `/compressor` redirect | Not started; last, after the github.io site is checked. The redirect pages exist. |

The old root `index.html` is gone already: rendering `index.qmd` writes over
it. It is in git history (commit `1083bfb`).

| Date | Question | Decision |

| 2026-10-19 | Spiritual Songs | Spiritual ≥ 1, and other songs can be added by hand. |
| 2026-10-19 | Google after the move | Retired. This repository is the only place songs are edited. |
| 2026-10-19 | Song page controls | Melody switch in phase 2; key menu later, in phase 5. |
| 2026-10-19 | Low and High columns | Kept as Andy's Voice, `voice_low` and `voice_high`, in scientific pitch (C4 = middle C). |
| 2026-10-19 | Optional fields | Every field but `title` is optional; `_templates/song.qmd` lists them all. |
| 2026-10-19 | Old spreadsheets | Copied into the repo as `.xlsx` files and linked from the song page. |
| 2026-10-19 | Songs to add | Moved to `_notes/songs-to-add.qmd`: in the repository, not on the site. |
| 2026-10-19 | Order of work | Phases 1–5 are built and checked at the github.io address. The domain moves last, in phase 6. |
